errors.sentence: I am writing to enquiry about the summer course.
errors.note: After “to”, the verb: to enquire. “Enquiry” is the noun.

errors.sentence: The aim of this report is assessing the new library.
errors.note: The aim … is TO + verb: “The aim of this report is to assess …”

errors.sentence: There is no doubt what the internet has changed our lives.
errors.note: “There is no doubt THAT …” – that, not what.

errors.sentence: If you are looking for a relaxing place, so Casa Velha can be an ideal choice.
errors.note: “If you are looking for …, THEN … can be an ideal choice.”

errors.sentence: Have you ever wonder what life was like without electricity?
errors.note: Present perfect: have you ever + past participle – wondered.

errors.sentence: Another aspect worth to mention is the friendly staff.
On the other side, it could be argued that exams cause stress.
errors.note: The fixed phrase is “on the other hand”.

errors.sentence: This is largely due to the fact what prices have risen.
I would be grateful if you can send me more information.
errors.note: “I would be grateful if you COULD …” – would and could go together.

errors.sentence: A recurring complain was that the showers were cold.
errors.note: “Complaint” is the noun; “complain” is the verb.

errors.sentence: Why don't you to come and stay with us?
I look forward to hear from you.
errors.note: “Look forward to” + -ing: I look forward to hearing from you.

errors.sentence: All things considering, I believe the benefits are greater.
errors.note: The fixed phrase is “all things considered”.

errors.sentence: In light with these findings, it is recommended that more benches be installed.
errors.note: The fixed phrase is “in light of”.

errors.sentence: I wouldn't hesitate recommending it to anyone.
errors.note: “Hesitate TO do”: I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it.

errors.sentence: Please don't hesitate to contact with me if you need anything.
To top it all of, the views are breathtaking.
errors.note: The phrase is “to top it all off” – off, with two f’s.

errors.sentence: On the whole, respondents were satisfied about the opening hours.
